items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: Dorothy Allen, Gray and Diane, and Kay Starr.

ctx.x: Yeah, yeah. I remember I met him in

New York in '49. "Melody Parade," 1944, directed by Lewis D. Collins. Universal Music featurette, 15 minutes. Spotlighting Charlie Barnet and His Orchestra and a stage setting, entertaining, with support from the Pied Pipers, June Hutton -- well, June Hutton would be in the Pied Pipers, right? Dorothy Allen, Gray and Diane, and Kay Starr. Numbers included, "How Am I to Know," "Redskin Rhumba," "Skyliner," -- it wasn't Les Cowan -- and "Washington Whirligig."

items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: I believe she replaced Kay Starr, if I'm not mistaken.

ctx.x: When did Fran Warren sing sign with you?

Fran came later. I think it was around -- oh, '46, around there. We played the Aquarium in New York, and I actually remember interviewing her at the Strand Theater. I believe -- I believe she replaced Kay Starr, if I'm not mistaken.
And Kay sang with you what, then, in '46, or '45?
